text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Chinese security tightened ahead of Deng Xiaoping's funeral on Tuesday in Beijing.
- Singapore moves up in world's export ranking list.
- Helicopters pluck 93 people from top floor of blazing 36-storey building.
- Singapore is rated second most competitive business location after United States/Canada.
- Port of Singapore Authority offers to build Philippine port.
- Only a third of private units in major developments launched in fourth quarter sold by end of 1996.
- Price war erupts in semiconductor foundry or wafer fabrication business with average prices expected to fall by over 30 percent this year.
- Monorail planners want to link malls in Marina Centre and Bugis Junction and trying to attract Singapore Bus Service and Trans-Island Bus Services for Singapore $70 million project.
- 43 percent of U.S. citizens own shares according to first detailed survey of retail investors since 1990.
- Amcol managers to sell off shares of joint venture company with Roland Maurel to try to recoup Amcol Holdings' US$39.6 million investment.
- Telekom Malaysia Bhd will spend about Malaysian $5 billion on developing its telecommunications infrastructure for country's Multimedia Super Corridor project until 2005.
